title: Cuban Communists
capsule: This entity represents the Popular Socialist Party (PSP, Partido Socialista Popular), the Cuban communist organization that operated under that name from 1944 onward, having originated as the Communist Party of Cuba in the 1920s and renamed itself for electoral reasons. During 1958–1960, the PSP initially maintained cautious distance from Fidel Castro's guerrilla campaign but aligned with the revolutionary government after Batista's fall on 1 January 1959. In July 1961, the PSP merged with Castro's 26th of July Movement and the Revolutionary Directorate to form the Integrated Revolutionary Organizations (ORI), which evolved into the United Party of the Cuban Socialist Revolution in 1962 and ultimately the Communist Party of Cuba on 3 October 1965 — the institution that still governs Cuba. The 1958–1960 window captures the transitional moment when the PSP shifted from peripheral actor to co-founder of the new state.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The PSP's political history is well-documented; its representation as a territorial entity in this dataset is atypical — political parties do not have mapped territories — so any geographic polygon assigned likely reflects provisional post-revolutionary control zones rather than formal boundaries.
